title: Section algebras and restriction charts of projective polarizations
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a projective finite-type $k$-scheme [def-kun-projective, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] such that some positive tensor power is the pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ under a closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$. Put $S=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}H^0(X,L^{\otimes m})$, with tensor-product multiplication [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. Then $S$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra and every $S_m$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. For every homogeneous $s\in S_d$ with $d>0$, its nonvanishing open $X_s$ is affine of finite type over $k$, and the fraction map $S_{(s)}\to\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_X)$, $a/s^n\mapsto a|_{X_s}/s^n|_{X_s}$, is an isomorphism; here $S_{(s)}$ is the degree-zero part of $S[1/s]$. For every closed subscheme $Y\hookrightarrow X$, the restriction $H^0(X,L^{\otimes m})\to H^0(Y,L^{\otimes m}|_Y)$ is surjective for all sufficiently large $m$. These conclusions allow nonreduced and disconnected schemes.

source.place: Tag 0B5T, lemma-coherent-proper-ample, parts (1), (3), (4); high-degree restriction is part (4) applied to the coherent ideal of Y and its cohomology exact sequence. Charts: morphisms.tex Tag 0C6J, lemma-proper-ample-is-proj, and Tag 0EKE, lemma-proper-ample-delete-affine. The positive-power embedding hypothesis is the projective polarization convention.

proof.text: Choose the given positive power r and closed immersion j. The uniqueness isomorphism between the tensor pullback adjunction and the usual pullback adjunction converts the specified polarization isomorphism to twistRestrict(j,1) ≅ L^r. This gives IsAmple(f,L). Pull back the coordinate sections: their nonvanishing opens are the inverse images of the standard affine opens, and they cover X. The comparison of zero-scheme support with the stalkwise nonvanishing locus includes empty and nonreduced schemes.

Every L^m is invertible and hence coherent. Apply the existing projective coherent cohomology finiteness theorem through an embedding of f, then the degree-zero cohomology isomorphism, to obtain finiteness of each S_m for the precise structural k-action in the statement.

Let p: O_X^(ι) → L^r be evaluation at the pulled-back coordinate sections. On each coordinate open one of these sections is a free generator, so p is epi. Its kernel K is quasi-coherent and of finite presentation on the locally Noetherian scheme X. Tensoring its kernel sequence by L^n is exact because tensoring by an invertible object is an equivalence. Serre vanishing gives H^1(K tensor L^n)=0 for n≥M. Therefore global sections of p tensor L^n are surjective. Decompose a section of the finite free source using its coordinate projections and the left unitor. After the tensor-power addition isomorphism, every section t in S_(r+n) is a sum Σ_i a_i b_i with b_i in S_n.

Give the direct sum its graded k-algebra structure explicitly: constants act through the structural map k→Γ(X,O_X) in degree zero, and the unitors prove compatibility with tensor multiplication. Choose finite k-spanning families in degrees n<r+M, and adjoin these together with the finitely many a_i. Strong induction on n proves every homogeneous section belongs to this subalgebra: low degrees follow by linear-span induction, and high degrees use the recurrence of the preceding step and n−r<n. Direct-sum induction then proves the subalgebra is the entire ring. This proves finite type without assuming S_0=k or generation in degree one.

For s in S_d, d>0, tensor the coordinate sections to exponent d and transport them through (L^r)^d ≅ (L^d)^r. Their affine nonvanishing opens are unchanged and still cover X. Apply the existing source-library theorem isAffineOpen_compl_support_zeroLocus (Modules.AffineComplement) to this cover and s^r, using properness of f. Positive tensor powers have the same nonvanishing locus, hence X_s is affine. X is Noetherian, so its open X_s is quasi-compact; the open immersion followed by f is locally of finite type and quasi-compact.

The restricted s is a free generator on X_s. The coefficient-hom theorem constructs the canonical map from homogeneous localization with precisely the numerator equation in the statement. The section-ring localization bijectivity theorem applies since X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Turn this same map into a ring equivalence using bijectivity; its fraction equation is unchanged, including zero localizations and the empty open.

For a closed immersion i, its coherent defining ideal I has vanishing H^1(I tensor L^m) for m sufficiently large by Serre vanishing. The closed-immersion unit-kernel theorem identifies the kernel of the chosen pullback adjunction unit on L^m with the image of ideal multiplication. Since L^m is invertible, that multiplication is mono, so this image is isomorphic to I tensor L^m. The cohomology exact sequence gives surjectivity of the unit on global sections. Finally the canonical uniqueness isomorphism between this adjunction and tensorPullbackSectionAdjunction carries one unit to the other; its pushforward is an isomorphism on sections, preserving surjectivity.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B5T(1),(3),(4): finite generation via the coordinate evaluation kernel and Serre vanishing, rather than the residue-class Proj comparison. Affineness uses the proved affine-complement theorem; localization uses coefficient and bijectivity theorems.

lean.statement: theorem projectivePolarizationSectionAlgebra (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [IsHProjective f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hpol : ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (j : X ⟶ ProjectiveSpace ι (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))), IsClosedImmersion j ∧ j ≫ (ProjectiveSpace ι (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) = f ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, 0 < r ∧ Nonempty ((tensorPullback j).obj (ProjectiveSpace.twist ι (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) ≅ L.tensorPow r)) : (∃ ρ : k →+* InvertibleSectionRing L, (∀ c : k, ρ c = DirectSum.of (SectionRingComponent L) 0 (unitSectionsEquiv ⊤ (f.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv c)))) ∧ ρ.FiniteType) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, @Module.Finite k (SectionRingComponent L m) _ _ (Module.compHom (SectionRingComponent L m) (f.appTop.hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom))) ∧ (∀ (d : ℕ), 0 < d → ∀ s : sectionRingGrade L d, ∃ U : X.Opens, (U : Set X) = nonvanishingLocus (L.tensorPow d) (s.val d) ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (U.ι ≫ f) ∧ QuasiCompact (U.ι ≫ f) ∧ ∃ e : HomogeneousLocalization.Away (sectionRingGrade L) s.val ≃+* Γ(X, U), ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : sectionRingGrade L (n • d)), e (HomogeneousLocalization.Away.mk (sectionRingGrade L) s.property n a.val a.property) • (L.tensorPow (n • d)).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).op ((s.val ^ n) (n • d)) = (L.tensorPow (n • d)).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).op (a.val (n • d))) ∧ (∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (i : Y ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i → ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → Function.Surjective (fun t : SectionRingComponent L m ↦ ((tensorPullbackSectionAdjunction i).unit.app (L.tensorPow m)).app ⊤ t))
